speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me which part of your leg or hip hurts the most, and did you have any recent injury or fall?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain feel like it is coming from your hip joint deep in the groin, or is it strictly in the knee? I need to check if moving your hip causes pain in your knee, which is a common referred pain pattern.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain in your knee change or worsen when I rotate your hip or move your leg at the hip joint? I want to determine if this is referred pain from the hip, which is common in conditions like Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain get worse after physical activity or at the end of the day? I am trying to distinguish between mechanical causes like Osgood-Schlatter disease and inflammatory conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine your hips now. Please lie down and let me check the range of motion in your left hip, specifically looking for any pain or restriction when I rotate it inward.
